title: Quietest time to visit Santorini (and how to avoid the crowds)
author: Brogan
intro: Late April, May and October are the quietest times to visit Santorini while it's still warm and open. November to March is quieter still, but many hotels and restaurants close. Here's how the year compares, and how to dodge the crowds on any day.
seo_title: Quietest time to visit Santorini: May and October
seo_description: Late April, May and October are quiet but warm and open. Winter is emptier but many hotels close. Month by month, plus cruise days and the Oia sunset.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Quiet and warm:** May and October
- **Quietest of all:** November to March
- **Busiest:** July and August
- **Busiest place:** Oia at sunset

Santorini gets crowded for two reasons: holidaymakers staying on the island, who peak in summer, and cruise passengers, who come ashore for the day from spring to autumn. Picking the right month deals with the first; picking the right time of day deals with the second.

sections.heading: Santorini month by month
sections.text:
| Months | Crowds | Daytime high | What's open |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nov to Mar | Very quiet | 14 to 19°C | Fira and some villages; many hotels closed |
| April | Quiet | about 19°C | Most places reopening |
| May | Fairly quiet | about 23°C | Almost everything |
| June | Busy | about 27°C | Everything |
| July and August | Busiest | about 29°C | Everything |
| September | Busy | about 26°C | Everything |
| October | Fairly quiet | about 22°C | Almost everything |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our [Santorini guide](/destinations/santorini). The sea is warmest from July to September, so May and October swims are bracing.

sections.heading: The cruise ships
sections.text:
Much of Santorini's daytime crowding comes from cruise ships, which anchor in the caldera and send passengers ashore by tender to Fira's old port. On a busy day, the queues for the cable car up from the port can be long, and Fira's lanes and Oia's paths fill up by mid-morning.

Greece has started to limit this. Santorini has a cap of about 8,000 cruise passengers a day, and passengers who go ashore pay a fee: €20 in the summer season, less in spring and autumn, and €4 in winter.

Tip: cruise schedules are published in advance. Before you book an excursion day to Oia or Fira, look up how many ships are due that day, and save the busiest days for the beach or a boat trip.

sections.heading: How to avoid the crowds on any day
sections.text:
- **Go early:** Oia and the caldera paths are calm before about 9am, and the light is beautiful.
- **Watch the sunset somewhere else:** Oia's castle is packed every evening. Imerovigli, Firostefani or a sunset boat trip are calmer, with views just as good.
- **Walk from Fira to Oia:** the caldera path takes about three to four hours, and much of it is quiet even in summer.
- **Stay outside Fira and Oia:** Imerovigli, Pyrgos or the beach villages are quieter in the evening.
- **Visit Akrotiri at lunchtime:** the covered Bronze Age town is a cool break when the villages are busiest.

Watch out: the caldera path has little shade and is very exposed in July and August. Start at dawn and carry plenty of water.

sections.heading: Is winter worth it?
sections.text:
From November to March, Santorini is very quiet. It suits a short, slow trip, but there are trade-offs:

- **The good:** prices drop sharply, Fira stays open, and the caldera views are the same. Walks, wineries and long lunches are all easier.
- **The catch:** many hotels, restaurants and boat trips close, and the sea is too cold for most people.
- **Getting there:** there are few or no direct flights from the UK in winter. Most visitors fly via Athens, then take a short flight or the ferry.
- **The weather:** mild by UK standards, at 14 to 19°C, but often windy, with some rain.

Santorini's wineries grow vines in low, basket-shaped coils to protect the grapes from the wind, and many stay open for tastings in the shoulder months.

sections.heading: Quieter islands nearby
sections.text:
If you want the Cyclades feel without Santorini's crowds, look at its neighbours:

- [Milos](/destinations/milos), for the white rocks of Sarakiniko and boat trips to Kleftiko.
- [Naxos](/destinations/naxos), for long sandy beaches and mountain villages.

Our post on [alternatives to Santorini](/blog/alternatives-to-santorini) compares more options, and the [holidays in Greece](/destinations/holidays-in-greece) page lists every Greek island we cover.

sections.heading: So, when should you go?
sections.text:
For warm weather, an open island and fewer people, go in **May** or **October**. For the emptiest island and the lowest prices, go in winter and accept that it's a slower trip. If you can only go in July or August, stay outside Oia, go out early and plan around the cruise days.

Still choosing between islands? Read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or add your shortlist to somewhere.party and let the draw pick. Our [Crete or Rhodes](/blog/crete-or-rhodes) post compares two bigger Greek islands.

faqs.question: What is the quietest month to visit Santorini?
faqs.answer: January and February are the quietest, but many hotels and restaurants close. For a quiet trip with everything open, go in May or October.

faqs.question: When is Santorini most crowded?
faqs.answer: July and August, especially in Oia at sunset and on days when several cruise ships call.

faqs.question: Is Santorini worth visiting in October?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's about 22°C by day, the crowds have thinned and nearly everything is still open, though the sea is cooling down.

faqs.question: How do you avoid the cruise crowds in Santorini?
faqs.answer: Check how many ships are due before you plan your day, visit Oia and Fira early in the morning, and save busy cruise days for the beach or a boat trip.
